h: Welcoming Shabbos as Both Bride and Queen

p: The holy Zohar on this parashah (III 272b) says:
the masters of the Mishnah would go out
Come, O bride! Come, O bride!"
the reading for Rabbi Chanina is:
to greet the bride, the queen";
"to greet Shabbos, the bride, the queen."
Come, O bride! Come, O bride!"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ
according to what the holy Zohar writes afterward:
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בֵּיצָה טז, א)
This is along the lines of what they said (Beitzah 16a):
which was given to them privately,
'Between Me and the Children of Yisrael
it is a sign forever,'" etc.
He did not make known to them";
He did not make known to them,
דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ וְכוּלֵּי
as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said," etc.
כִּי אֲנִי ה׳ מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם (שָׁם לא, יג)
that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you" (ibid. 31:13):
that Hashem Yisbarach gives on Shabbos
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת י, ב)
About this they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 10b):
and I wish to give it to Yisrael," etc.
into the heart of a person;
in the aspect of Matronisa and queen,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים ב)
as written in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Parashas Kedoshim 2):
"Since you have been sanctified to My Name," etc.,
just as I am holy," etc.
"Since you have been sanctified to My Name,
I am king and you are queen;
just as this is My honor,
so it is your honor," etc.
between Me and you for your generations,
to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you":
that Hashem Yisbarach, on His part,
Therefore they said about this in the Midrash
with a queen sitting opposite him;
And this is what the Gemara says:
"Its reward He did not make known to them."
The second is the extra soul
for the service of Hashem Yisbarach.
in the holy Zohar cited above:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יח)
as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people," etc.
שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָז
For when Dovid HaMelech, alav hashalom, saw then
"Keep this forever as the inclination," etc.:
that the longing that Yisrael have
And this is called the extra soul;
הַנֵּר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
"the lamp of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27);
"Your word is a lamp to my feet
and a light for my path."
for the service of Hashem Yisbarach;
and this is called the aspect of a bride,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מוֹעֵד קָטָן כה, ב)
as we find in the Gemara (Moed Katan 25b):
And about this too it says,
"Between Me and the Children of Yisrael
it is a sign forever," etc.,
And this is what the Gemara says:
"The extra soul He did not make known to them."
מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בֹּאִי כַלָּה בֹּאִי כַלָּה
their saying "Come, O bride! Come, O bride!"
"a wise man's heart is at his right,
and a fool's heart is at his left" (Koheles 10:2).
For "the yetzer tov that descends on Shabbos"
implies that there descends from Heaven
to "a wise man's heart, at his right,"
and the service of Hashem Yisbarach;
and to "a fool's heart, at his left,"
that he will want to rectify the foolish heart
so that it too will be good,
that the inclination be only for good.
it is found in Pri Etz Chaim
to say "Come, O bride, Shabbos the queen"
And it is found in the holy sefarim
and the third time corresponds to Daas;
Chochmah corresponds to "a wise man's heart, at his right,"
and he will return and be healed";
שֶׁהוּא לְתַקֵּן הַלֵּב כְּסִיל גַּם כֵּן
which is to rectify the foolish heart as well.
And the third time we say quietly,
for it corresponds to the aspect of Daas,
which is the joining of Chochmah and Binah,
and it is the inwardness from Kesser Elyon;
Therefore we then say "Shabbos the queen":
is called in the aspect of queen;
in the Midrash Tanchuma cited above:
"Just as I am king, you are queen";
are bound up in the beginning of Thought.
would wrap himself and stand," etc.,
"and say: Come, let us go out
And also, why did he say it in the plural?
of the yetzer tov that descends on Shabbos,
to the wise heart and to the foolish heart,
of the extra soul should come.
that is, let us go out entirely
from the matters of the body,
which is the aspect of divesting from physicality,
so that we not feel at all
As is found in the Mechilta
that it should be as though
from all matters of this world.
For about Shabbos it is found in the holy Zohar
that it is a day of souls
and not a day of the body at all.
that is, to the two levels,
"and let us go out" from all matters of the body,
which is the aspect of divesting from physicality;
"to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you":
also in the aspect of Malchus:
for through their accepting upon themselves
the yoke of the Kingship of Heaven,
for there is no king without a people.
with a queen sitting opposite him,"
And this is what is written
in the holy Zohar cited above:

Welcoming Holiness Into Both Sides of the Heart
Going Out to Greet the Queen

paragraphs.text: Source: Shabbos 113b — “… של חול. דבור אסור, הרהור — מותר. בשלמא כולהו — לחיי, אלא שלא יהא הילוכך של שבת כהילוכך של חול מאי היא? כי הא דאמר רב הונא אמר רב, ואמרי …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 238) — “means that your speech on Shabbat should not be like your speech during the week, i.e., one should not discuss his weekday affairs on Shabbat. However, it is only speech that they said is prohibited, whereas merely contemplating weekday affairs …”
